dimensions.name: Spec & environment reconnaissance

evidence.note: Opens by probing the runtime environment: checks /app state, Python version and available tools before building — genuine environment reconnaissance.
Downloads the three vendored libraries and verifies their hashes rather than assuming — confirms the hard pinning constraint against reality.
Verifies stdlib modules available, confirming offline/dependency assumptions before major coding.

Task decomposition encodes extracted constraints: full endpoint surface (OAuth/PKCE, scopes, timelines, lists, polls), CSP, Mastodon purple, and exact seed minimums (>=8 accounts, >=20 statuses, CWs, media) — shows a working model of the wire contract and verifier requirements.
Returns to constraints mid-build with security-header and anti-cheat compliance checks, but as verification during construction rather than up-front gate enumeration.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent extracted the explicit hard constraints (vendored-lib hashes/paths/versions, CSP, seed minimums, full endpoint list) and formed a working model of the Mastodon API surface before major coding, and additionally probed the runtime environment (Python, tools, stdlib, offline deps) and verified hashes rather than assuming — placing it above the level-5 anchor. It stops short of level 8: there is no visible deliberate reconciliation against the real Mastodon contract, no explicit enumeration of the 19-gate categories, and no confirmed check of the canary-strip detail. Confidence is low because the trajectory is only a titles index, so richer reconnaissance in the hidden prose cannot be ruled out.

dimensions.name: Subsystem breakdown & milestone sequencing

evidence.note: Foundations-first ordering: environment recon, dep install, and vendored-library hash download/verify (step 6) precede any feature code; storage/util (db.py, util.py) written before endpoints — a dependency-aware build order.

Agent explicitly created four subsystem milestones via TaskCreate in dependency order: (1) ASGI/routing/OAuth-PKCE/sessions/serializers, (2) accounts/statuses/timelines/faves/reblogs/notifications/search/media/polls/lists, (3) templates/CSS-purple/CSP, (4) seed/start.sh/_health/verify. Foundations (auth, storage) sequenced before features and UI.

Milestones marked in_progress→completed as work advanced, with completion following verification runs (e.g. task completed at step 106 only after extensive smoke/API/OAuth/anti-cheat tests in steps 66-105), showing done-checks tied to milestones rather than pure aspiration.

TaskList reviewed and final task marked complete at end, indicating the milestone list was maintained through to closure — but the four milestones remained coarse (task 2 lumps ~13 features) and show no explicit encoded verification hooks or scope revision.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained a genuinely dependency-aware ordered plan — deps+hash-verify → storage → auth/app → API features → UI+CSP → seed/verify — with foundations front-loaded and milestones tracked in_progress/completed against verification runs, clearly clearing the level-5 'sensible ordered plan, foundations before features' bar. It stops short of level 8 because the milestones are coarse (four buckets lumping dozens of components), carry no explicit per-item done-criteria encoded in the plan, and show no visible revision as scope reality emerged. This places it at a 6: better-than-sensible sequencing with completion gated on verification, but not the calibrated, hook-bearing, self-revising hierarchy of the higher anchors.

dimensions.name: Designing checks against the wire contract & gates

evidence.note: Downloads the three vendored libraries and verifies their hashes at build time — directly mirroring the SHA256 pin gate.
Systematically checks security headers, full OAuth+PKCE flow, anti-cheat compliance, ETag cache validators, idempotency, and scope enforcement — the knowable verifier surface.
Verifies landing-page seed visibility, seed minimums (CW and media posts), visibility icons, and Post button label — realism and seed-count gates.
Tests pagination, polls, reports/audit, cookie security attributes, and scope/CSRF — including subtle failure modes like cookie handling.
Repeatedly re-runs and re-tests after fixing 500s, marker handling, and avatar/seed issues — closing the loop rather than declaring done.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent goes well beyond the level-5 'main flows work' bar: it validates against essentially the entire knowable verifier (hash pins, CSP/headers, OAuth+PKCE, scopes, anti-cheat, seed minimums, palette/button-label/visibility-icon realism, durability/idempotency) matching the level-8 anchor, and adds client-shaped checks (ETag cache validators, pagination), subtle-failure probing (cookie attributes, CSRF), and consistent re-verification after each fix — hallmarks of level 10. It falls just short of a clean 10 because the checks appear as ad-hoc Bash/curl invocations rather than a reusable repeatable suite, and some client shapes (error JSON, offline runtime-fetch) aren't explicitly named. Confidence is medium because the condensed log shows targets but not the depth of each observation.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across a wide surface

evidence.note: Created an explicit 4-task ledger via the Task tool, each task enumerating a cluster of subsystems (auth/API/UI/seed), establishing a tracked done-vs-remaining structure rather than pure mental tracking.
Marched task states in_progress→completed in dependency order across the whole build, showing sustained (not abandoned) ledger use over the long horizon.

Broad systematic verification sweep covering nearly every subsystem (OAuth/PKCE, scopes, idempotency, ETag, pagination, polls/reports/audit, markers, relationships, headers, cookies, CSRF, seed/CW/media), evidencing accurate coverage awareness across the wide surface.
Detected and resolved stuck states (500 debugging, marker JSON-vs-form) without extended circular looping, though ledger was coarse rather than tracking each item as verified/pending.
Re-listed tasks near the end to reconcile status before final completion.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent kept and continuously updated an explicit ledger and ran a comprehensive subsystem-by-subsystem verification sweep, giving an accurate view of what was built vs remaining and catching several stuck points before recovering — clearly above the 'usable running checklist' anchor (5). However, the ledger was coarse (4 milestone tasks) and fine-grained coverage was tracked implicitly through ad hoc tests rather than an explicit per-endpoint/per-gate verified-vs-pending status with deliberate time-boxing, keeping it short of the granular self-reconciling rigor of 8. This lands at 6.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: On repeated 500s the agent diagnoses root cause (checks server log, tests whether env globals reach macros, tries rendering the macro in isolation) then edits web.py and re-verifies via restart — appropriate diagnose-and-adjust rather than blind retry.
markers endpoint with JSON body fails; agent edits api.py and re-tests with form-encoded input — a clean contract/content-type mismatch correction.
Seed-coverage shortfalls (CW, media, avatars) diagnosed by inspecting the DB, then fixed in seed.py and re-run to confirm — targeted correction of falsified assumptions about seed data.

Hash verification done at download and JS vendored as static files from the outset, so the CSP-inline and hash-mismatch pitfalls were pre-empted rather than hit — no whole-approach redesign was ever forced.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently reacts to failing checks (500s, JSON-vs-form contract mismatch, seed shortfalls) by diagnosing the cause, applying a targeted fix, and re-verifying — squarely the anchor-5 behavior. It never pushes a broken premise (above 0/3), but there is no observed instance of recognizing an entire approach as falsified and deliberately restructuring it (anchor 8), partly because early architectural choices pre-empted the CSP/hash crises. Corrections stay local and well-targeted, so the observed level sits at 5.

dimensions.name: Kill-switch gate triage & de-risking

evidence.note: Immediately after installing deps, downloaded the vendored libraries AND verified their hashes — front-loading the cheapest-but-fatal gate (exact SHA256/path/version pins) before any app code was written.

Ran 'anti-cheat compliance' checks twice, once mid-build and again near the end, showing the 5 anti-cheat rules were treated as a guarded surface re-verified as the build evolved, not a one-time assumption.
Explicitly checked security headers (CSP gate), cookie attributes (HttpOnly/SameSite), and scope/CSRF — locking down the strict-CSP and auth-plane binary requirements with concrete checks.
Sustained seed-minimum triage: landing-page visibility, seed coverage, CW-count, media-count, and idempotent re-seed — verifying the seed-minimum gates rather than assuming them.
Verified the compose Post-button label and visibility icons — targeting the button-label kill-switch and realism-gate constraints specifically.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent front-loaded the vendored-library hash gate at step 6 and then ran targeted verification passes across nearly the entire kill-switch surface — anti-cheat rules (twice), CSP/headers, cookies, seed minimums, and the Post-button label — verifying each rather than assuming, which matches the level-8 anchor of explicit cost/fatality triage with front-loading and confirmation. It falls short of 10 because the (title-only) evidence shows no explicit palette RGB measurement, hash-recompute with the canary-strip caveat, or a fully enumerated managed risk register.

rubric.task_read: Chirp is an enormous, long-horizon build: a Mastodon-v1-API-compatible self-hosted service plus a server-rendered HTMX/Alpine/SSE web UI, spanning OAuth2+PKCE, dual auth planes, durable storage, dozens of API endpoints, admin/lists/polls/media/notifications, and a realism-graded UI — verified by 19 pytest gates plus multiple binary kill-switch gates (exact SHA256-pinned vendored libs at exact paths, anti-cheat scans, strict CSP, brand palette, button labels, seed-data minimums). Difficulty comes from breadth (many independently-verified sub-systems), wire-contract fidelity to an external spec, and numerous cheap-but-fatal constraints that fail the whole trial up-front. This is the high end for every meta-work faculty: allocation, sequencing, and continuous verification decide whether the agent sustains coverage across the surface or thrashes.

dimensions.name: Spec & environment reconnaissance
dimensions.description: Building an accurate map of the Mastodon wire contract, the exact verifier constraints (hashes/paths/versions, anti-cheat rules, CSP, gates, seed minimums), and the runtime environment before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task hides its real requirements across a dense spec and an external protocol; acting before extracting the exact pins, gate shapes, and API shapes guarantees rework and up-front trial failures.

anchors.0: Starts coding a generic chat app with no reading of the spec, protocol, or constraints; misses that Mastodon compatibility or specific pins even exist.
anchors.3: Skims the task; picks up a few obvious items (start.sh, /_health) but never pins down exact SHA256/paths/versions, gate semantics, or Mastodon endpoint shapes before building.
anchors.5: Extracts the explicit hard constraints (vendored-lib paths+hashes+versions, CSP rules, seed minimums, endpoint list) and forms a working model of the Mastodon API surface before major coding.
anchors.8: Deliberately reconciles the spec against the real Mastodon contract and the verifier's stated checks — enumerates the 19-gate categories, the 5 anti-cheat rules, and the realism gates; probes the environment (Python version, offline behavior, curl access) and confirms the hash-strip/canary detail rather than assuming.
anchors.10: Sustained, self-correcting research: continually returns to the spec as new endpoints/edge cases surface (pagination, cache validators, scopes, visibility rules), verifies assumptions against real Mastodon client expectations, and resolves ambiguities (e.g. compressed-time env vars, dual auth planes) with evidence rather than guesses — leaving a clear, referenced understanding that de-risks the whole build.

dimensions.name: Subsystem breakdown & milestone sequencing
dimensions.description: Decomposing a sprawling build into an ordered hierarchy of subsystems (storage → auth → API → UI → SSE → admin → seed → realism polish), each with an explicit done-check, in a dependency-aware order.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With this many independently-verified components, an undifferentiated push loses coverage; correct sequencing (durable storage and auth before endpoints, vendored libs+CSP before UI) prevents late-stage rework and abandoned surface area.

anchors.0: No structure; codes whatever comes to mind with no ordering, leaving whole subsystems (admin, lists, notifications, seed) untouched or discovered too late.
anchors.3: A vague or flat list of features with no dependency ordering and no per-item done-criteria; milestones are aspirational, not checkable.
anchors.5: A sensible ordered plan covering the major subsystems with rough done-criteria and a defensible build order (foundations before features).
anchors.8: Dependency-aware milestones each with an explicit verification hook (e.g. 'auth done = token issues + introspection returns active; UI done = CSP passes + no inline scripts + palette in range'); early milestones de-risk foundations that everything else depends on.
anchors.10: A living, well-calibrated milestone hierarchy that maps the full surface, sequences to retire the highest-risk dependencies first, sizes each chunk to a verifiable increment, and is explicitly revised as scope reality emerges — never ceremony, always driving the next concrete check.

dimensions.name: Designing checks against the wire contract & gates
dimensions.description: Proactively building and running checks — health, OAuth flows, endpoint behavior against Mastodon shapes, hash verification, CSP/header inspection, seed-count checks, UI realism — beyond just 'it starts'.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Much of the verifier is knowable (hashes, gate categories, seed minimums, header rules), so a skilled agent can build tests toward those checks; assuming success on a 19-gate + binary-gate surface is how trials silently fail.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes endpoints and UI work because code was written; never runs the service or checks a single response.
anchors.3: Runs the server and hits /_health or the homepage, but does not exercise OAuth, endpoint contracts, hashes, headers, or seed counts.
anchors.5: Verifies the main flows end-to-end (token issuance, a post, a timeline, a follow) and confirms the service boots and serves the UI; spot-checks a few constraints.
anchors.8: Systematically validates against the knowable verifier: recomputes the three SHA256 pins at the exact paths, inspects CSP/security headers, exercises OAuth+PKCE and scope enforcement, confirms seed minimums and realism specifics (palette, button label, visibility icons), and tests durability across restart.
anchors.10: Treats verification as first-class and continuous: builds repeatable checks (scripts/curl suites) mirroring the gates, verifies Mastodon-client-shaped responses (pagination Link headers, cache validators, error JSON), catches the subtle failure modes (CSP blocking Alpine, cookie in URL, offline runtime fetch), and re-verifies after changes — closing the loop rather than declaring done.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across a wide surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate done-vs-remaining picture across dozens of endpoints and constraints, and detecting stuck/circular states over a very long horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is far larger than fits in working memory; without an explicit ledger the agent silently drops subsystems (introspection, lists, admin audit, CW media) or loops on one hard bug while the rest rots.

anchors.0: No sense of overall progress; repeatedly forgets what's built, re-touches finished areas, or ends leaving large swaths unaddressed without noticing.
anchors.3: Loose mental tracking only; drops or double-covers items and doesn't notice being stuck until much later.
anchors.5: Keeps a usable running checklist of subsystems/constraints and updates it, giving a roughly accurate view of what remains.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, granular status of the full requirement set (endpoints, gates, realism items, seed targets), marks each verified vs pending, and recognizes when a subsystem is thrashing and time-boxes it.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise, continuously-reconciled picture across the whole horizon — knows exactly which of the 19 gate areas and binary gates are proven vs open, allocates remaining effort by risk/coverage, detects circular debugging early and redirects, and never loses the plot on the large surface.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design/approach when reality diverges — CSP breaking inline JS, hash mismatch, client incompatibility, auth-plane conflicts, contract mismatches — instead of pushing ahead on a broken premise.
dimensions.why_it_matters: This build is full of tight, interacting constraints (strict CSP vs HTMX/Alpine, offline vs CDN, dual auth planes) where the first approach often violates a gate; recovering requires genuine redesign, not brute force.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps retrying a fundamentally broken approach (e.g. inline scripts under strict CSP, runtime CDN fetch) until it fails.
anchors.3: Reacts to hard errors with local patches but doesn't revisit the underlying design when a patch can't hold.
anchors.5: When a check fails, diagnoses and adjusts the approach appropriately (moves JS to files, fixes hash path, corrects a header) and moves on.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a whole approach is falsified and redesigns deliberately — e.g. restructuring UI JS to satisfy no-unsafe-inline while keeping HTMX/Alpine/SSE working, or reworking auth to cleanly split API-bearer from UI-session — and re-verifies the change.
anchors.10: Fluidly updates the design/plan as evidence accumulates, distinguishing local fixes from structural ones, feeding corrections back into milestones and the requirement ledger, and pre-empting cascading failures (e.g. anticipating that a CSP or vendoring decision affects every page) rather than rediscovering them repeatedly.

dimensions.name: Kill-switch gate triage & de-risking
dimensions.description: Identifying the cheap-but-fatal binary gates (exact vendored-lib hashes/paths/versions, 5 anti-cheat rules, strict CSP, brand palette, button label, seed minimums, offline requirement) and front-loading/guarding them so the trial isn't failed up-front regardless of functional quality.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The verifier fails the whole trial before the rubric runs if any gate fires; these are largely low-effort but unforgiving, so a skilled agent triages them by fatality-vs-cost and locks them down early — a distinct risk-prioritization demand created by this task's gate structure.

anchors.0: Oblivious to the binary gates; e.g. edits the vendored files, uses a js/ subdir or wrong version, ships unsafe-inline, or picks a non-purple accent — dooming the trial without realizing.
anchors.3: Aware some constraints are hard but treats them ad hoc; discovers gate violations late or leaves risky ones unverified.
anchors.5: Identifies the major fatal gates and satisfies them (correct pinned files/paths, purple accent, allowed button label, strict CSP), checking most before finishing.
anchors.8: Explicitly triages the full kill-switch set by cost and fatality, front-loads the cheap-but-fatal ones (vendoring pristine downloads to exact paths, offline serving, seed minimums, no build-tool artifacts), and verifies each is actually satisfied rather than assumed.
anchors.10: Systematically enumerates every binary gate, proves each with a concrete check (recomputed hashes with the canary-strip caveat, header scans, palette measurement, anti-cheat surface audit, offline runtime confirmation), and keeps them guarded against regression as the build evolves — treating the gate surface as a managed risk register, not a one-time pass.
